newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South Africa's industrial and all-share indices were boosted by a firm rand on Monday, but golds slipped on the strength in the currency and a weaker bullion price.
Dealers said futures players were active in the market and there was good demand.

"It has been a good market...The market turned around sharply and there has been a good demand for shares. Bullish factors are there and the rand is stronger," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack.
Dealers said volumes were high, boosted by 200 million in a corporate finance deal. The stronger rand also augured well for foreign buying in the country.
Although a rate cut was not anticipated until the end of the second quarter, dealers said pre-emptive buying also helped shares.
Golds were largely ignored and weakened on the strength in the currency.
The market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street on Tuesday.
The overall index rose 37.5 points to 6,713.6, the industrial index gained 58.6 points to 8,061.9 points and the gold index shed 11.0 points to 1,339.0 points.

Shares in Suncrush Ltd and Amalgamated Beverage Industries Ltd climbed on Monday on news that U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola Co would invest 1.25 billion in South Africa over the next five years, dealers and analysts said.
Coca-Cola said it intended to double its business in South Africa as a result of the investment which would be split on a 50-50 basis between Coca-Cola and its bottlers.

Q Data shares also climbed to 10.50 rand, a 30 cent gain, buoyed by better-than-expected results released early this morning, dealers said. They said there was still upward potential for the share price with its P.E. ratio at 48.
Near-term equity futures were mixed in active trade, with currency and bond market enthusiasm spilling over to industrial contracts and golds limp on a dull bullion price and a better rand.
The March all share contract was at 6,130/35 from 6,104, the industrial contract was at 7,808/15 from 7,769 and the gold contract was at 935/944 from 938 previously.
